pages.title: RADOS Object Catalog: metadata pool and data pools

features.name: Object naming from inode numbers
features.description: Per-inode objects are named "%llx.%08llx" of (ino, object number or raw frag_t), with a ".inode" suffix for base inodes; tables use mds<r>_inotable, mds_snaptable, mds<r>_sessionmap, mds<r>_openfiles.<hex idx>; all MDS metadata objects live in the metadata pool's default namespace.
features.notes: Data-object naming is shared with clients; metadata-object naming is MDS-private but hard-coded in offline tools.

features.name: Striped data and journal object mapping
features.description: Byte offsets map to objects with Striper::file_to_extents (stripe_unit, stripe_count, object_size); object count via get_num_objects; default layout 4 MiB/1/4 MiB.
features.notes: Clients and MDS must agree exactly; the MDS uses it for purge, truncate, probe, journals.

features.name: Special inode numbers and per-rank system inode ranges
features.description: Root=1, .ceph=2 (legacy), global snaprealm=3 (in-memory), lost+found=4 (tools), mdsdir 0x100+r, journal 0x200+r, alternate journal 0x300+r, journal pointer 0x400+r, purge queue 0x500+r, strays 0x600+10r+i, system base 0x1000; InoTable range [(r+1)<<40, (r+2)<<40).
features.notes: kclient rejects inode numbers in [0x100,0x1000) with -EREMOTEIO (linux/fs/ceph/inode.c:184); LOOKUPINO on them returns ESTALE.

features.name: Dirfrag omap storage
features.description: Each directory fragment is one metadata-pool object <dirino>.<frag>: omap header = fnode_t ENCODE_START(4,3), one omap key per non-null dentry; frag_t() object also carries the directory backtrace xattrs.
features.notes: Requires omap: metadata pool must be replicated (mon enforces).

features.name: Dentry omap key format with snapshots
features.description: Key "<name>_head" for live dentries, "<name>_<last snapid hex>" for snapshotted dentries; decode splits at the last underscore and asserts if none.
features.notes: Names are client-provided (charmap-folded or fscrypt base64); originals in alternate_name.

features.name: Primary dentry with embedded inode ('i' / legacy 'I')
features.description: Value = u64 first + 'i' + ENCODE_START(2,1){alternate_name, InodeStore ENCODE_START(6,4){inode_t v20, symlink, fragtree, xattrs, snap_blob(sr_t), old_inodes, oldest_snap, damage_flags}}; 'I' = bare InodeStore (still written by cephfs-data-scan).
features.notes: Inodes have no object of their own; attributes, xattrs, symlink target, inline data, quota, pins, charmap/quarantine optmetadata, snaprealm (incl. subvolume flag) and snapshot history live in the parent dirfrag value. CDir::_load_dentry does not copy the embedded damage_flags into the CInode (rewritten as 0 on the next commit); the dirfrag commit writes the symlink string only when non-empty while decode keys it on S_ISLNK.

features.name: Remote dentry for hard links ('l' / legacy 'L')
features.description: Value = u64 first + 'l' + ENCODE_START(2,1){u64 ino, u8 d_type, string alternate_name}; legacy 'L' = u64 ino + u8 d_type.
features.notes: Resolving a remote dentry to its primary may need a backtrace (open_ino with metadata-pool hint for DT_DIR). Linking outside a subvolume also gives the target inode its own snaprealm (sr_t with PARENT_GLOBAL) stored in its primary dentry's snap_blob.

features.name: Inode and snaprealm on-disk encodings
features.description: inode_t ENCODE_START(20,6) field order incl. client_ranges, dirstat/rstat, old_pools, inline_data, quota, export pins, flags, fscrypt fields and optmetadata (CHARMAP, QUARANTINE); sr_t ENCODE_START(8,4) with flags PARENT_GLOBAL/SUBVOLUME/SNAPDIR_VISIBILITY; SnapInfo ENCODE_START(4,2).
features.notes: Layout encoding depends on MDSMap up features (legacy vs v2).

features.name: Dirfrag fetch (full, paged, keyed, background)
features.description: omap_get_header + paged omap_get_vals (mds_dir_keys_per_op, OSD caps 1024/reply) or omap_get_vals_by_keys when mds_dir_prefetch=false, optional background full prefetch; restart if a commit completed mid-fetch; header-only fetch for stray dirfrags at boot.
features.notes: Read errors other than ENOENT/ENODATA fail ceph_assert in _omap_fetched (src/mds/CDir.cc:2063); an undecodable frag-0 parent xattr throws from verify_diri_backtrace (no try).

features.name: Dirfrag commit (incremental, batched, header-last, no blind create)
features.description: Writes only dirty dentries (full rewrite for new fragmenting frags), split into ops of at most mds_dir_max_commit_size, header in the last op, stat guard unless the dirfrag is new; encoded on the finisher without mds_lock; one commit in flight per dirfrag.

features.name: Stale snapshot dentry trimming
features.description: When fnode.snap_purged_thru < realm last_destroyed, snapped dentries covering no live snapshot are skipped on load and their keys removed on the next commit.

features.name: Dentry corruption detection and damage isolation
features.description: first > last or first > next snap -> damaged dentry; undecodable value -> damaged dentry; missing/corrupt fnode -> damaged dirfrag (EIO), fatal for root and own strays; damage to own mdsdir/stray dentries fatal; exceeding mds_damage_table_max_entries fatal.

features.name: Base inode objects (.inode)
features.description: Root and per-rank mdsdir inodes are stored as write_full of magic "ceph fs volume v011" + InodeStore in <ino>.00000000.inode; legacy 'inode' xattr fallback on read; missing/corrupt -> rank damaged.

features.name: mkfs of a new rank (up:creating)
features.description: Creates journal header + pointer (async), root (rank 0) with backtrace, mdsdir with 10 stray dirs (each with backtrace), InoTable, empty SessionMap, PurgeQueue header, SnapTable (tableserver), then journals ESubtreeMap.
features.notes: Mon requires an empty metadata pool at fs new; stopped ranks restart with up:starting reusing their objects.

features.name: Boot-time object loading
features.description: Existing ranks load inotable, sessionmap, journal pointer/header (+forward probe), purge queue, OFT (async), snaptable (tableserver), mdsdir and root base inodes; replay never reads dirfrags; later phases fetch undefined dirfrags, stray headers, OFT prefetch, backtraces.

features.name: Stray directories per rank
features.description: Ten stray dirs per rank (0x600+10r+i) linked as primary dentries stray0..stray9 in the mdsdir dirfrag; stray dentries named by hex inode number; stray dirs are fragmentable, mdsdir and dirs inside strays are not.
features.notes: Needed for POSIX unlink-while-open semantics, hard links and snapshot retention.

features.name: Backtrace xattr ('parent') on object 0
features.description: inode_backtrace_t ENCODE_START(5,4){ino, ancestors[(dirino,dname,version)], pool, old_pools} written as xattr 'parent' on <ino>.00000000: metadata pool for dirs, layout pool (always default namespace) for files.
features.notes: Not read by any client; required by the C++ MDS for lookup-by-ino after cache loss and by cephfs-data-scan.

features.name: Layout and symlink xattrs on object 0
features.description: 'layout' (file_layout_t, up-features encoding) on the current pool's object 0 for every inode; 'symlink' target when mds_symlink_recovery (default true).
features.notes: Consumed by cephfs-data-scan to rebuild layouts, dir layouts and symlinks.

features.name: Backtrace copies in the default data pool and old pools
features.description: Files created in a non-default pool add the default data pool to old_pools; layout changes add the old pool; with STATE_DIRTYPOOL the backtrace is written to every old pool with pool=current, enabling redirection.
features.notes: _stored_backtrace treats ENOENT as success only when the current backtrace pool is gone; results are shared per pool batch (BatchStoredBacktrace).

features.name: Directory backtrace verification on fetch
features.description: With mds_verify_backtrace>0 the frag-0 fetch also reads 'parent' and checks ancestors[0]; mismatch re-dirties the backtrace (assert if >1).

features.name: Lookup by inode number via backtraces (open_ino)
features.description: Uncached inode lookup: ask peers, then read 'parent' from the default data pool or hinted pool, follow bt.pool, retry metadata pool on ENOENT, open ancestors recursively; empty ancestors -> ESTALE.
features.notes: Backs NFS file handles (LOOKUPINO, LOOKUPHASH, LOOKUPPARENT, LOOKUPNAME), hard links, reconnect of uncached caps.

features.name: Scrub tag xattr
features.description: Tagged scrub writes 'scrub_tag' on each inode's backtrace object (creating it if missing); cephfs-data-scan filters by it via the cls_cephfs PGLS filter cephfs.inode_tag (names ending .00000000).

features.name: InoTable object
features.description: mds<r>_inotable = u64 version + ENCODE_START(2,2){interval_set free}; write_full at mkfs, segment expiry, mds_skip_ino at replay_done and scrub repair of an inode wrongly marked free; any load error damages the rank.

features.name: SnapTable object
features.description: mds_snaptable = u64 version + SnapServer ENCODE_START(5,3){last_snap, snaps, need_to_purge, pending_*, last_created, last_destroyed, snaprealm_v2_since} + pending_for_mds map outside the envelope; only on the tableserver rank (0); last_snap seeded from pool snap_seq.
features.notes: first-damage.py reads raw byte offsets 8 and 14..22.

features.name: SessionMap omap object
features.description: mds<r>_sessionmap: omap header ENCODE_START(1,1){version}; key client.<id> -> session_info_t ENCODE_START(7,7) (inst, completed_requests, prealloc_inos, completed_flushes, auth_name, client_metadata); full save at expiry, save_if_dirty for completed requests; legacy blob format readable.
features.notes: completed_requests persistence enables idempotent replies to retried client requests after failover.

features.name: Session metadata threshold eviction
features.description: Sessions whose encoding reaches mds_session_metadata_threshold (16 MiB) are not saved but evicted (blocklisted if mds_session_blocklist_on_evict).
features.notes: Perf counter mds_sessions.mdthresh_evicted.

features.name: OpenFileTable objects with journaled commit
features.description: mds<r>_openfiles.<hex>: header magic + ENCODE_START(1,1){omap_version, num_objs, journal_state}; key %llx ino -> Anchor + u32 0; multi-object updates use _journal.N keys with START/FINISH states; up to 1024 objects x 200000 keys; tail objects never deleted; load errors only drop prefetch hints.
features.notes: Performance-only recovery hints.

features.name: MDLog journal objects
features.description: Journaler over <front>.<n>: header object 0 (magic, trimmed/expire/write pos, legacy layout, stream format), data from offset = period, RESILIENT framing with sentinel 0x3141592653589793 and start offset; payload u32 0 + ENCODE_START(1,1){type, event}; prezero, trim and erase via Filer.

features.name: JournalPointer and journal reformat
features.description: <0x400+r>.00000000 = ENCODE_START(1,1){front, back}; created at mkfs (async) or recovery; back != 0 during reformat between 0x200+r and 0x300+r; standby-replay refuses (EAGAIN) while back is set; front may stay 0x300+r.

features.name: PurgeQueue journal and purge execution
features.description: <0x500+r>.* Journaler (RESILIENT) of PurgeItem ENCODE_START(2,1){action, ino, size, layout v2, old_pools, snapc, fragtree, stamp, pad}; PURGE_FILE removes data objects + object 0 (default ns) + old-pool backtraces with the realm snapc; TRUNCATE_FILE keeps object 0; PURGE_DIR removes leaf frags + frag 0.
features.notes: Deleted files free space asynchronously. Purge-op errors other than EBLOCKLISTED are ignored (item still completes, src/mds/PurgeQueue.cc:604-614); journal errors make the queue read-only and call MDSRank::handle_write_error.

features.name: Data object truncation by the MDS
features.description: After journaling a size reduction the MDS issues CEPH_OSD_OP_TRIMTRUNC (truncate_seq, in-object offset) on affected objects (filer_max_truncate_ops in flight); fscrypt last block is rewritten first; segment expiry waits.
features.notes: Works with clients sending truncate_seq/size on every data op; a TRIMTRUNC/write result other than 0/ENOENT fails ceph_assert (src/mds/MDCache.cc:6617, 6632).

features.name: File size recovery by probing data objects
features.description: When a client with writable ranges is lost, RecoveryQueue probes (STAT) objects backwards from max_size to recover size and mtime.

features.name: Delegated inode cleanup on session close
features.description: Inos delegated to a client for async creates and unused at session close: remove object 0 using the default file layout, journal EPurged, release to InoTable; unused preallocated inos released without IO.
features.notes: FIXME in code: non-default pools/namespaces not handled; a remove result other than 0/ENOENT fails ceph_assert (src/mds/MDCache.cc:6909).

features.name: Inline data uninlining
features.description: Scrub-driven internal op writes inline data into object 0 guarded by cmpxattr inline_version GT and sets inline_version to CEPH_INLINE_NONE; clients run their own uninline with the same xattr.

features.name: Snapshot block diff via list_snaps
features.description: CEPH_MDS_OP_FILE_BLOCKDIFF lists snapshot clones of data objects (list_snaps at SNAP_DIR, up to 16 concurrent) to compute changed extents.
features.notes: Used by snapshot mirroring/diff consumers.

features.name: Mantle balancer object
features.description: Lua object named by MDSMap::balancer is read synchronously from the metadata pool (timeout mds_bal_interval/2) when the name changes.

features.name: Data-pool snapshot id allocation and removal
features.description: SnapServer allocates snapids above every data pool's snap_seq, persists them in mds_snaptable, and asks the monitor (MRemoveSnaps) to remove deleted snaps from data pools.

features.name: Fragmentation object lifecycle
features.description: Split/merge commits new frags in full, then removes old frag objects (frag_t() is truncated and omap-cleared to keep backtrace xattrs), bracketed by EFragment PREPARE/COMMIT/FINISH.
features.notes: Old-frag removal tolerates only 0/ENOENT (ceph_assert, src/mds/MDCache.cc:12255).

features.name: Directory size limits tied to omap
features.description: Every dirfrag is capped at mds_bal_fragment_size_max (100000) head entries (ENOSPC); split at mds_bal_split_size (10000); root, mdsdir, ino 2 and dirs inside strays are never fragmented (root since 2025). The same cap applies to the target stray dirfrag, so unlink/rename-over return ENOSPC when it is full.
features.notes: Keeps omap objects below the OSD LARGE_OMAP thresholds.

features.name: Lazy writeback at log segment expiry
features.description: Dirfrags, base inodes, backtraces (batched per pool on the finisher), InoTable, SessionMap, SnapTable, OFT commit, truncates and purges are completed before a segment expires and the journal is trimmed.

features.name: Version-gated idempotent replay against stored tables
features.description: Replay compares journaled inotablev/sessionmapv/tablev with loaded object versions and skips or force-applies; dirfrags are never read during replay.

features.name: Metadata write error policy
features.description: Write errors: EBLOCKLISTED -> respawn; otherwise mds_action_on_write_error (1 = read-only, >=2 respawn, 0 ignore); PurgeQueue errors make the queue read-only.

features.name: Inode numbers are never reused
features.description: Purged inodes are not returned to the InoTable; only unused preallocated/delegated inos are released. Exception: delegated inos released at session close only had object 0 in the default data pool removed, so objects an async-create client wrote elsewhere can alias a later file with that number.
features.notes: Keeps data-object names and NFS handles from aliasing newer files.

features.name: Legacy on-disk formats still readable
features.description: 'I'/'L' dentries, base inode in 'inode' xattr, legacy SessionMap blob, OFT 13-byte header, journal format 0 (rewritten), PurgeItem v1 (13.2.2 bug layout), 'stray' dentry, byte-swapped frag_t.
features.notes: Irrelevant for a non-backward-compatible MDS.

features.name: Offline repair tools over the on-disk format
features.description: cephfs-journal-tool, cephfs-table-tool, cephfs-data-scan (incl. pg_files), first-damage.py, cephfs-meta-injection and ceph-dencoder read/write the exact formats.
features.notes: Documented in doc/cephfs/disaster-recovery-experts.rst. cephfs-data-scan never sets a RADOS namespace (data under pool_ns is invisible to scan_extents); cephfs-meta-injection amend writes first + JSON marker + encode_bare (only valid as 'I').

features.name: Shared metadata pool with mgr-owned objects
features.description: snap_schedule stores snap_db_v0 (namespace cephfs-snap-schedule, legacy dump read once and removed) and a libcephsqlite DB snap_db_v0.db striped as <file>.<16 hex> in the default namespace (rollback-journal naming unverified); mirroring stores cephfs_mirror (omap dir_map_*, instance_*, sync_stat/*; watch/notify).

features.name: Pool preconditions enforced by the monitor
features.description: fs new requires an empty metadata pool (unless --force), non-EC metadata pool, no mon-managed snaps, EC data pools with overwrites, --force for EC default data pool; tags pools with application cephfs.

features.name: Assert-on-error metadata and data IO paths
features.description: Several completions accept only 0/ENOENT (or ENODATA) and otherwise abort the MDS instead of recording damage: dirfrag reads, truncate ops, old-frag purge, delegated-ino purge; EBLOCKLISTED/ETIMEDOUT are intercepted first and respawn.
features.notes: Unexpected OSD errors (EIO, quota/full errors) crash the rank rather than degrade it.

features.name: Scrub-time InoTable and backtrace repair writes
features.description: Scrub with repair rewrites backtraces (mark_dirty_parent) and saves the InoTable when an in-use inode is marked free.

serialization_points.name: mds_lock around all metadata-object IO completions
serialization_points.shared_state: Entire MDS cache and all backing-object state machines
serialization_points.why_serialized: Every RADOS completion (dirfrag fetch/commit, inode store, backtrace, tables, sessionmap, OFT) re-takes the global mds_lock on the finisher thread
serialization_points.notes: Completions of unrelated subtrees/dirfrags serialize on one lock.

serialization_points.name: One in-flight commit per dirfrag
serialization_points.shared_state: committing_version/committed_version of a CDir and its RADOS object
serialization_points.why_serialized: Header-last protocol and version accounting assume ordered, non-overlapping commits per object
serialization_points.notes: Ordering per object is inherent; waiting for the previous commit before starting the next is not.

serialization_points.name: Segment expiry gather
serialization_points.shared_state: All objects dirtied by a log segment
serialization_points.why_serialized: Journal can only be trimmed past a segment once every dirtied object, OFT commit, truncate and purge it references is durable
serialization_points.notes: Unrelated subtrees are coupled only because they share one per-rank journal.

serialization_points.name: Single MDLog stream per rank
serialization_points.why_serialized: All mutations of a rank are encoded and appended by one submit thread to one byte stream

serialization_points.name: Journaler internal lock and write-buffer throttle
serialization_points.why_serialized: Single byte stream with ordered flushes and prezero ahead of write_pos
serialization_points.notes: Inherent per stream; with per-shard streams the scope becomes the shard.

serialization_points.name: InoTable whole-object rewrite
serialization_points.why_serialized: One write_full of the entire free set per save and one version per rank
serialization_points.notes: Allocation could be range-partitioned per shard.

serialization_points.name: SessionMap single header version and save op
serialization_points.shared_state: mds<r>_sessionmap header version and dirty session set
serialization_points.why_serialized: All sessions of a rank share one header version and are written in one op

serialization_points.name: SnapTable on the tableserver rank
serialization_points.why_serialized: Snapids must be unique and above every data pool snap_seq; one server rank owns allocation
serialization_points.notes: Global ordering of snapids is inherent for shared data pools; a single object/rank is not.

serialization_points.name: Single OpenFileTable commit
serialization_points.why_serialized: num_pending_commit==0 asserted; commit tied to the last log seq; expiry waits for it

serialization_points.name: PurgeQueue single journal and in-order expiry
serialization_points.why_serialized: expire_pos can only advance over contiguous completed items

serialization_points.name: PurgeQueue push under mds_lock
serialization_points.why_serialized: StrayManager::purge runs under mds_lock and appends synchronously to the PQ journal buffer
serialization_points.notes: Can block mds_lock on the Journaler write-buffer throttle (~3.5 GiB).

serialization_points.name: Fragmentation of a directory
serialization_points.why_serialized: EFragment prepare/commit/finish around full rewrite of new frags and removal of old ones

serialization_points.name: Mantle balancer synchronous read
serialization_points.why_serialized: Blocking read with timeout mds_bal_interval/2 while holding mds_lock
serialization_points.notes: Only when the balancer name changes.

serialization_points.name: JournalPointer and journal recovery blocking IO
serialization_points.why_serialized: Recovery thread performs blocking load/save/erase before boot can proceed

serialization_points.name: Log trim upkeep under mds_lock issues all writeback
serialization_points.shared_state: Segment list and all dirty cache objects
serialization_points.why_serialized: mds-log-trim thread holds mds_lock while expiring segments and triggering every backing-object write and the OFT commit

serialization_points.name: Backtrace construction needs a stable ancestor chain
serialization_points.shared_state: Primary parent chain from the inode to the root
serialization_points.why_serialized: Backtrace built at expiry under mds_lock by walking cached parents
serialization_points.notes: True conflict only with renames of ancestors.

serialization_points.name: Per-pool backtrace batch completion
serialization_points.shared_state: Dirty-parent state of every inode whose backtrace was batched for one pool in one segment expiry
serialization_points.why_serialized: All backtrace ops for a pool are gathered; the first error and the completion of the slowest op are delivered to every inode of the batch
serialization_points.notes: Independent inodes share failure and latency only because they are batched per pool.

serialization_points.name: Blocking JournalPointer write under mds_lock at the end of a journal reformat
serialization_points.shared_state: JournalPointer object (back = 0) and the MDLog journaler pointer
serialization_points.why_serialized: The recovery thread takes mds_lock and performs a synchronous write_full of the pointer before swapping journalers
serialization_points.notes: Only during boot after an old-format journal is rewritten.

external_contract.detail: Objects "%llx.%08llx" of (ino, objectno) in (layout.pool_id, layout.pool_ns) with Striper mapping; computed by the client from inode number and layout.
Same naming via Striper/Filer; ceph-fuse and NFS-Ganesha (via libcephfs) inherit it.
Inode numbers in [0x100, 0x1000) are rejected (-EREMOTEIO) and skipped in NFS handle decode and quota.

external_contract.item: Root and global snaprealm inode numbers
external_contract.detail: Root is ino 1; the global realm ino 3 is pinned by the client.

external_contract.item: Root and global snaprealm inode numbers
external_contract.detail: Client::get_snap_realm pins realm 3; mount root is ino 1.
Client issues STAT and exclusive CREATE of <ino>.00000000 in the file's pool/namespace once per (pool, ns); object 0 may exist for empty files.
Same probe in Client::check_pool_perm.
New inodes start (1, -1); clients attach truncate_seq/size to every data op; MDS bumps the seq and issues TRIMTRUNC.
(1,-1) means no truncation; newer seq on write applies pending truncation; stale writes clipped; TRIMTRUNC ignored on missing objects or non-newer seq.
Uninline uses cmpxattr GT/U64 on inline_version of object 0 then sets the decimal version.
Same protocol in Client uninline.
Operand decoded as LE u64; stored value parsed as decimal; empty xattr = 0.

external_contract.item: Lookup by inode number must survive MDS cache loss
external_contract.detail: NFS export ops LOOKUPINO/LOOKUPPARENT/LOOKUPNAME for uncached inodes.
LOOKUPHASH / LOOKUPINO / LOOKUPPARENT / LOOKUPNAME requests.
dl_dir_hash and the 24-bit frag space are used by clients for frag choice and readdir; dirfrag object names are not visible.
fscrypt long names (truncated + SHA-256 key, full ciphertext in alternate_name) and charmap originals are stored per dentry and returned.
Metadata relies on omap header/keys, xattrs, stat-guarded compound ops, per-object ordering, FAILOK, create(excl/non-excl), list_snaps.
Each omap_get_vals reply is capped at osd_max_omap_entries_per_request (1024) entries or osd_max_omap_bytes_per_request (1 GiB).

Deep scrub warns above 200000 keys or 1 GiB per object; OFT sharding stays below the key threshold; mds_bal_fragment_size_max bounds only head dentries, so snapshotted name_<snap> keys can push a dirfrag over it.
OMAPRMKEYS/OMAPCLEAR return ENOENT on missing objects; ZERO is a no-op; SETXATTR/OMAPSET create the object.

external_contract.item: Self-managed snapshot SnapContexts on data pools
external_contract.detail: Purges remove data objects with the realm SnapContext so clones survive.
SnapServer sends MRemoveSnaps for deleted snapids in data pools.

external_contract.item: Empty metadata pool at fs new
external_contract.detail: fs new refuses a metadata pool with objects unless --force.
Metadata pool not EC, no mon-managed snaps; EC data pools need overwrites; EC default data pool needs --force (backtraces).

external_contract.item: On-disk format compat features in MDSMap
external_contract.detail: Incompat features 4,6,8,9,10,11,12 describe this format and gate which MDS daemons may join.
snap_db_v0 (ns cephfs-snap-schedule) and libcephsqlite snap_db_v0.db objects in the default namespace.
Omap-based directory map (dir_map_*), instance registry (instance_*) and sync statistics (sync_stat/<fs>/...) with watch/notify.
Admin stores Lua in the metadata pool and names it with ceph fs set <fs> balancer.

Pointer, Journaler header/entries, dirfrag values, .inode objects, InoTable; recover_dentries writes 'i'/'l' dentries (and with --alternate-pool removes recovered keys from 4.00000000); journal reset --force rewrites the pointer and a fresh header.
Data objects (default RADOS namespace only), object-0 xattrs (parent/layout/symlink/scan_*), dirfrags, tables, lost+found; writes 'I' dentries with CEPH_NOSNAP first sentinel.
mds<r>_inotable, mds_snaptable, mds<r>_sessionmap show/reset/take_inos.
Reads first 8 bytes of every dentry value and mds_snaptable byte offsets; reports bad first, removes with --remove, rewrites CEPH_NOSNAP first on _head keys with --repair-nosnap.

Decodes fnode_t, inode_t, InodeStore(Bare), backtraces, InoTable, SnapServer, PurgeItem, JournalPointer, Journaler::Header and most journal events (not EPurged, ENoOp, ELid, ESegment, SessionMapStore).

rust_implications.topic: Data-pool object naming is not free
rust_implications.implication: Unmodified clients compute "%llx.%08llx" data-object names from the inode number and layout and write them directly; the Rust MDS must hand out layouts and inode numbers under exactly the C++ Striper semantics, and every purge/truncate/probe must use the same mapping.

rust_implications.topic: Inode number allocation constraints
rust_implications.implication: Inode numbers are 64-bit, root must be 1, 3 is treated as the global snaprealm by clients, [0x100,0x1000) is rejected by kclient; numbers must never be reused while data objects or NFS handles may exist. Per-shard (subvolume) disjoint ranges are compatible with clients; the C++ per-rank 2^40 ranges are not client-visible.

rust_implications.topic: Metadata pool is shared and starts empty
rust_implications.implication: fs new requires an empty metadata pool, but mgr modules later create snap_db_v0*, cephfs_mirror and possibly other objects in it; the Rust MDS should place its objects under a dedicated RADOS namespace or unambiguous prefix and never assume it owns every object when listing or recovering.

rust_implications.topic: Metadata pool has omap, data pools may not
rust_implications.implication: Only the metadata pool is guaranteed replicated/omap-capable; anything the Rust MDS stores in data pools (if anything) must be object data or xattrs, and EC data pools need overwrites.

rust_implications.topic: Lookup-by-ino index is required
rust_implications.implication: NFS-Ganesha and kernel nfsd file handles and LOOKUPINO/LOOKUPHASH/LOOKUPPARENT must resolve inode numbers that are not cached, across restarts and failovers. The C++ MDS uses backtraces; a Rust MDS can instead maintain its own persistent ino -> (shard, parent, name) index in the metadata pool, avoiding per-file writes to data pools.

rust_implications.topic: Purge must cover client-created objects
rust_implications.implication: Object 0 can exist for empty files (pool permission probe) and objects can exist up to max(size, max_size, max_size_ever); purge must remove them in the layout's pool and namespace with the inode's SnapContext, and must also handle delegated-but-unused inos in the pool/namespace the client used (C++ has a FIXME here).

rust_implications.topic: Truncate semantics are an OSD/client contract
rust_implications.implication: Clients send truncate_seq/truncate_size on every data op and the OSD applies TRIMTRUNC idempotently per seq; the Rust MDS must keep truncate_seq starting at 1 with size -1, bump it on shrink, and issue TRIMTRUNC to all affected objects (fscrypt last-block rewrite included).

rust_implications.topic: File size recovery needs object probing
rust_implications.implication: When a client holding writable ranges dies, size/mtime must be recovered by stat-probing data objects up to max_size; this is per-inode and fully parallelizable.

rust_implications.topic: Snapshot ids remain a global allocator
rust_implications.implication: Snapids are used in SnapContexts against shared data pools and must exceed pool snap_seq and be ordered for every object; per-subvolume shards can only get disjoint pre-reserved ranges from one global allocator, and removals still go to the monitor via MRemoveSnaps.

rust_implications.topic: Per-shard journals replace the per-rank stream
rust_implications.implication: The C++ MDS couples unrelated subtrees through one Journaler stream, one segment expiry gather and one set of rank tables; per-subvolume journals (e.g. Journaler-like objects keyed by shard id) with independent expiry and parallel replay remove these non-inherent serialization points.

rust_implications.topic: Large directories need sharded objects
rust_implications.implication: OSD limits (1024 omap entries per read, LARGE_OMAP warning at 200000 keys/1 GiB, osd_max_write_size) still force directory sharding (dirfrag-like objects) for big directories, including the root, which C++ no longer fragments.

rust_implications.topic: Commit atomicity per object
rust_implications.implication: C++ relies on per-object op ordering and header-last commits plus a stat guard against blind recreation; a Rust design can use single atomic compound ops per object, or versioned omap keys, but must handle partial multi-op commits explicitly.

rust_implications.topic: Idempotent replay needs persisted versions
rust_implications.implication: Replay correctness in C++ depends on version numbers stored in table objects and dentry/inode versions; per-shard journals need an equivalent per-object or per-shard watermark so replay can skip already-applied updates.

rust_implications.topic: Offline tools will not work
rust_implications.implication: cephfs-journal-tool, cephfs-data-scan, cephfs-table-tool, first-damage.py, cephfs-meta-injection and ceph-dencoder hard-code the C++ formats and object names; documented disaster-recovery procedures will not apply, so the Rust MDS needs its own inspection/repair tooling and must not leave C++-looking objects that these tools could misinterpret.

rust_implications.topic: MDSMap compat set must still admit the daemon
rust_implications.implication: Monitors check the MDS beacon compat against the file system's MDSMap compat set, whose incompat entries name C++ on-disk features (dir inode in separate object, dirfrag in omap, snaprealm v2, minor log segments, ...); the Rust MDS must advertise a compat set the unmodified monitor accepts even though its on-disk format differs.

rust_implications.topic: Do not block a global lock on RADOS
rust_implications.implication: C++ blocks under mds_lock for the Mantle object read, PQ journal throttle and every IO completion; Rust workers should never wait on RADOS while holding shard locks.

rust_implications.topic: Backtrace-free design still needs disaster-recovery data
rust_implications.implication: If the Rust MDS does not write backtraces on object 0, losing metadata objects means data-pool contents can no longer be re-linked; consider a cheap per-file recovery xattr or a separately replicated ino index.

rust_implications.topic: Default data pool semantics
rust_implications.implication: C++ writes a backtrace for nearly every file into the default data pool (the reason mon discourages EC default data pools); a Rust MDS may skip this, but mon/mgr behavior around the default data pool is unchanged.

rust_implications.topic: Inline data can be disabled
rust_implications.implication: Inline data requires the inline_version xattr protocol shared with clients; a minimal Rust MDS can keep the MDSMap inline_data flag off so clients never create inline files, while still honoring existing client uninline attempts if any.

rust_implications.topic: Exactly-once request replies across failover
rust_implications.implication: C++ persists completed_requests per session in the SessionMap to answer retried requests idempotently; the Rust MDS needs equivalent per-session (possibly per-shard) persistence.

rust_implications.topic: Deferred deletion is POSIX-required
rust_implications.implication: Unlink of an open file and hard links require keeping inodes alive after the last name disappears (C++ stray dirs + PurgeQueue); Rust needs per-shard orphan lists and an asynchronous purger, not the C++ stray naming.

rust_implications.topic: Open-file hints are optional
rust_implications.implication: The OpenFileTable only accelerates recovery; a Rust MDS can rebuild hints from client reconnects, at the cost of slower recovery.

rust_implications.topic: Unexpected OSD errors should degrade, not abort
rust_implications.implication: The C++ MDS aborts on dirfrag read errors other than ENOENT/ENODATA and on truncate/old-frag/delegated-ino purge errors other than ENOENT, and silently ignores purge-op errors; a Rust MDS should classify OSD errors (fencing, full, EIO, missing object) per object and record damage or retry instead of crashing the rank or leaking objects.

rust_implications.topic: Clients do not validate everything the MDS stores
rust_implications.implication: libcephfs passes an empty symlink target through and the C++ MDS stores it with an encoding asymmetry; a Rust MDS must validate request payloads (empty targets, name lengths, alternate_name sizes) itself rather than rely on the kernel VFS checks that libcephfs/Ganesha paths bypass.

open_questions: MDCache::uninline_data_work builds the cmpxattr operand with in->encode(bl, version), i.e. InodeStoreBase::encode (full inode encoding with features=version), instead of a u64; intended guard or latent bug (src/mds/MDCache.cc:13550)?

CDir::_omap_commit_ops encodes *fnode on the finisher thread without mds_lock (src/mds/CDir.cc:2514-2516) while the dentry set and version were captured earlier; can the header carry a newer version than the dentries written, and is that benign?
PurgeQueue::_consume passes a partially decoded item to _execute_item after a decode error (src/mds/PurgeQueue.cc:522-530); could this issue removes for a bogus ino?

Backtraces for files with a non-empty layout pool_ns go to the pool's default namespace (src/mds/CInode.cc:1469); a file purged with max(size, max_size, max_size_ever)==0 only gets its default-namespace object 0 removed, so a client pool-permission probe object in pool_ns leaks. Code-path analysis: the kclient probe runs once per (pool, ns) per mount on the first Fr/Fw cap acquisition (linux/fs/ceph/caps.c:3071, addr.c:2581), so at most one object per mount and namespace; not reproduced.
MDCache::purge_inodes always uses default_file_layout for delegated-ino cleanup (FIXME in code); objects created by async-create clients in other pools/namespaces are not removed.
No code path deletes the objects of a stopped rank (mdsdir, strays, journal, purge queue, tables, OFT); is this intentional so the rank can restart with up:starting?
cephfs-data-scan still writes legacy 'I' dentries with first=CEPH_NOSNAP sentinels and OR-s DAMAGE_* enum values (0,1,2) as bit masks; any reason these were not updated?

Root directory fragmentation was disallowed in 2025 (commit f4bcf5bfd53) without a stated reason; root is therefore capped at mds_bal_fragment_size_max entries. What motivated it? Note MDCache::open_root/open_root_inode open and fetch only frag_t() of the root (src/mds/MDCache.cc:685-760); behaviour on a file system whose root was fragmented before the change is unverified.
first-damage.py hard-codes SnapServer struct_v 5 byte offsets; any change in mds_snaptable encoding breaks it.

mds_snaptable encodes pending_for_mds outside the SnapServer ENCODE_START envelope (src/mds/MDSTableServer.cc:353), so the envelope cannot be extended at its end without breaking readers; confirm expectations for tools.
CDir::_load_dentry never copies InodeStore::damage_flags into the CInode (src/mds/CDir.cc:1995-2012), so flags set by cephfs-data-scan on embedded inodes are lost on the next dentry commit; intended?

CDir::_encode_primary_inode_base writes the symlink only if non-empty (src/mds/CDir.cc:2435) while decode_bare keys on S_ISLNK; neither Server::handle_client_symlink nor libcephfs rejects an empty target. Can an empty-target symlink be created via libcephfs/NFS-Ganesha and corrupt its dentry? (unverified in practice)

optmetadata_singleton::get_kind returns kind 3 (== _MAX) unchanged and defconstruct_type indexes a 3-element table with it (src/include/cephfs/types.h:584, 566); decoding a future kind 3 is undefined behaviour.
CInode::verify_diri_backtrace decodes the frag-0 parent xattr without try/catch (src/mds/CInode.cc:1624); does an undecodable directory backtrace crash the MDS on dirfrag fetch?

_stored_backtrace checks pool existence against the current backtrace pool, so ENOENT from a deleted old pool (DIRTYPOOL copy) is treated as a write error (read-only by default) and is shared by the whole per-pool batch; is that reachable after fs rm_data_pool + pool deletion?
cephfs-meta-injection amend writes first + JSON itype + encode_bare and MetaTool::inode_meta_t::get_meta() returns NULL for 'i' parents; is the tool usable on current-format ('i') dirfrags?
